say: First, your code asks for the last hundred orders. One trip to the database.

say: Then for each order, it goes back to fetch the customer. One trip per order. A hundred more.

say: Every trip waits on the network and the database. Those small waits add up. That is the slow part.

say: This is the N plus one problem. One query for the list, then one query for each of the hundred orders. A hundred and one queries.
show: This is the N plus one problem. One query for the list, then one query for each of the hundred orders. A hundred and one queries.

say: The fix: get the orders, then ask for all their customers together in one query. Two trips total.
